faqs.question: Who should take this Ethical Hacking specialization?
faqs.answer: This is for people who already have some security or IT foundation and want to go deep into hands-on penetration testing — including graduates of our Cybersecurity Foundations course, IT professionals moving into security, and anyone serious about becoming a working ethical hacker.

faqs.question: Can I pay for just one step instead of the whole specialization?
faqs.answer: Yes! You can start with just one step for as little as ₦45,000. Each step has its own price, and you can add more whenever you're ready. If you're able to take the full specialization at once, it works out cheaper (₦370,000 instead of ₦450,000 if bought step by step) — but starting small is always an option.

faqs.question: Do I need to complete Cybersecurity Foundations first?
faqs.answer: It's not a hard requirement, but we strongly recommend it — or equivalent experience with basic networking, operating systems, and security concepts. This specialization moves fast and assumes that foundation is already in place.

faqs.question: Can I pick any step, or do I have to go in order?
faqs.answer: We strongly recommend going in order here, since almost every later step builds directly on the tools and techniques from Steps 1 and 2. You're still free to start wherever you like — if you skip ahead, we'll let you know clearly what you might want to brush up on first.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a Step Certificate and the Full Course Certificate?
faqs.answer: Every step you complete earns its own Digitanotion Step Certificate. Once you've completed all 6 steps, you also receive the Digitanotion Certified Ethical Hacker (DCEH) certificate — our CEH-aligned credential, recognised by our industry partners as full specialization completion.

faqs.question: What if I only finish a few steps? Do I lose anything?
faqs.answer: Not at all. You keep every Step Certificate you've earned, and you can come back and continue at any time — there's no deadline or expiry on picking up where you left off.

faqs.question: What tools will I learn to use?
faqs.answer: Industry-standard tools including Kali Linux, Metasploit Framework, Burp Suite, Nmap, Wireshark, SQLmap, John the Ripper, Hydra, Aircrack-ng, and the Social Engineering Toolkit — the same tools working penetration testers use every day.

faqs.question: Are the labs conducted in a safe environment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every lab runs in an isolated virtual environment with intentionally vulnerable systems built specifically for training. No real systems are ever touched, so you can practice real attack techniques without real-world consequences.

faqs.question: What career opportunities does this open?
faqs.answer: Graduates are ready for roles like Penetration Tester, Ethical Hacker, Vulnerability Assessment Analyst, Security Consultant, Security Auditor, SOC Analyst (Level 2/3), Incident Responder, and Security Engineer.

faqs.question: How much time should I set aside each week?
faqs.answer: About 12–15 hours a week: roughly 6 hours for live sessions, 6–8 hours for lab work, and a couple of hours for self-study. It's intensive, but structured so you actually master each stage before moving on.

faqs.question: What kind of projects will I work on?
faqs.answer: You'll complete a full network penetration test, a web application security assessment, a mobile security review, and — in the final step — a complete capstone project simulating a real corporate penetration test with a professional report.

faqs.question: What support is available during the course?
faqs.answer: A dedicated mentor with real industry experience, round-the-clock lab access, a technical support community, career counselling, resume and interview preparation, and access to our alumni job board.

faqs.question: Is this course suitable for beginners in cybersecurity?
faqs.answer: This is an advanced specialization, so it isn't the best starting point if you're completely new to cybersecurity. We recommend our Cybersecurity Foundations course first — it sets up everything this course builds on.
